subject: Re: MAP update — reconciliation, new guardrails, and sign-off
messages:
From: Karen Liu <karen@nimbus.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Evans <sam.evans@nimbus.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: MAP and close cadence — slipping risk on our side

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. We ran into an internal dependency (third-party security review) that will add a potential 2-3 week delay to our internal sign-off.

I attached the MAP we use (high level) and marked the impacted milestones. The pragmatic ask from our side: can Redwood provide a short remediation plan for how we handle a 2-week slip to the close date, including any SLA/commitment fallback and who from your side will own escalation if we hit that window?

Appreciate a clear owner and a proposed rebaseline so we can take to our CIO.

Best,
Karen
VP, Solutions
Nimbus

Attachment: Nimbus_MAP_v3.xlsx

-----
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Karen Liu <karen@nimbus.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and close cadence — slipping risk on our side

Karen — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the MAP. I reviewed the marked milestones and sketched an initial rebaseline with guardrails. Summary below; full attachment is the updated MAP (Nimbus_MAP_v3.xlsx).

High-level proposal (2-week slip):
- New target close: 2026-07-16 (previously 2026-07-02).
- Canary/fallback policy: keep a canary hosted instance running on a reserved slot for final validation day + 48 hours; if smoke tests pass we proceed to cutover, otherwise automatic rollback to the prior stable model snapshot.
- SLA exception: offer a one-time 30-day service credit cap tied to specific latency SLOs if production onboarding is delayed >14 days caused by Redwood capacity vs customer dependencies.
- Escalation owner (Redwood): Laura Bennett (Sr. PM, Partnerships) — contact laura_bennett@redwood.com for exec escalations.
- Procurement/Legal runway: we will route a redline review to Legal within 48 hours of final MAP sign-off; procurement questions captured in procurement_questions.pdf.

Risk register entries (short):
1) Security review delay at Nimbus — mitigations: provide security artifacts (audit logs, SOC2 docs) within 24 hours, offer dedicated review slot with infra team.
2) Capacity contention for dedicated pools — mitigations: reserve burst units for final validation window; if unavailable, fallback to hosted with throttled throughput.
3) Integration test failures — mitigations: define a short checklist before final day and a triage channel (Slack #nimbus-go-live).

Next steps / asks:
- Karen: confirm acceptability of the new target (2026-07-16) and canary policy by COB Wed 24 Jun.
- Nimbus procurement: confirm whether DocuSign routing can be paused for final redlines next week.
- Laura/Ben: mark any operational constraints from your side.

Thanks — I will schedule a 30-minute alignment call on Wed assuming acceptance.

—Olga
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Nimbus_MAP_v3.xlsx

-----
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP and close cadence — slipping risk on our side

Adding a couple of operational guardrails:
- Legal: if Nimbus proposes contract changes that affect uptime/penalty language we should escalate to Legal and Sales Ops before signing. I can be the initial intake but will loop Legal as needed.
- Procurement questions (I reviewed the PDF): I recommend we pre-clear three items before sign-off: data retention window, KMS key ownership, and audit log retention. If Nimbus cannot confirm, we should move to a conditional acceptance with a 30-day remediation plan.

Risk log entries to record now (for exec visibility):
- RISK-009: Close slip >10 days due to external security review — impact: onboarding delay, potential revenue recognition timing shift. Owner: Laura Bennett.
- RISK-010: Contract redline on SLA — impact: legal review cycle adds 7 business days. Owner: Ben Carter (Sales).

If the Nimbus CIO needs Exec-level reassurances I can join the Wed call.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, GTM
Redwood Inference

-----
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2026 14:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP and close cadence — slipping risk on our side

Quick note on capacity and commercials:
- We can reserve the burst slot for the validation window but it will consume 1 reserved unit for 48 hours. We should be explicit with Nimbus that this reservation is a billable add-on unless we convert to an annual Dedicated commitment — otherwise apply the one-time credit language Olga proposed.
- If Nimbus pushes pricing because of the slip, Sales is open to a modest concession (one month of reduced unit pricing) in exchange for a firm rebaseline and a signed MAP.

I'll be on the Wed call to finalize terms.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

-----
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Karen Liu <karen@nimbus.com>, Sam Evans <sam.evans@nimbus.com>, procurement@nimbus.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP update — reconciliation, new guardrails, and sign-off

Karen / Sam — following our internal alignment, attached is an updated MAP and a short risk log summary. Key asks: please confirm acceptance of the new target close (2026-07-16) and the canary fallback policy by EOD Mon 29 Jun so we can lock Legal/Procurement review windows. If that works I will push the DocuSign envelope (link below) with conditional acceptance terms.

DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/DocuSignLink/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/HS-48321

If Nimbus prefers to keep the original date we will need to escalate internally for additional reserved capacity and expedite legal — that will require sign-off from Sales leadership on potential credit exposure.

Thanks and speak soon,
Olga
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: procurement_questions.pdf
